To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of thin films of ionic conducting oxides affects the ionic conductivity by changing the lattice strain and the defect structure.
ionic diffusion in thin films depends on the processing history and the lattice-strain of the film.

the lattice strain of a thin film is not a constant but can change during the deposition and processing of a film and that the lattice strain can be measured by X-ray diffraction and can be used to predict and optimize the ionic conductivity of a thin film.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of lattice strain on the ionic diffusion of metal oxide thin film structures.
the influence of lattice strain and the degree of disorder on the ionic conductivity of electroceramic thin-films.
the correlation of lattice-strain to ionic diffusion for thin-film metal oxides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lattice strain is an important parameter to characterize ionic conducting thin-film materials and that the ionic conduction of thin films is no longer a question of bulk properties.
the lattice strain in the films is the key to the ionic diffusion and thus to the ionic conductivity.
lattice-strain is a matter of processing history for thin films, which can be used to tune their defect state, i.e. oxygen vacancies, and ionic diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ionic conductivity of metal oxide thin film materials is a matter of lattice strain.
the lattice-strain is a measure for the degree of disorder in ionic conducting metal oxide thin film microstructures.
lattice-strain is a measure for atomistic defects that can affect the ionic conductivity of thin films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lattice-strain is an important parameter to be considered when designing electroceramic devices based on thin films.
the processing history, i.e. synthesis route, determines the lattice strain and thus the ionic conductivity.

lattice strain is a key factor to be discussed when it comes to ionic conductivity of metal oxide thin film systems and it is suggested to measure lattice strain in addition to other characteristics such as the average grain size and the degree of crystallinity.
